questionsToConsider: Will answers be anonymous? For a small team, say plainly who will read them and whether names are shown.
Do you want to compare with last time? Keep the grid rows the same every retro so the trend means something.
How long before the meeting should people answer, so the facilitator has time to group the replies?
Did the team agree on actions last time? Consider adding a question about whether they happened.
guide.howToUseResponses: Before the meeting, group the slowed-down answers and the try-next ideas into themes, and bring the top two or three into the room rather than reading every reply. Use the comparison grid to show whether last retro's actions made a difference. If several people score low on speaking up, raise it carefully as a team topic, not an individual one, and agree on no more than two actions with a named owner each.
customizeSteps: Edit the slowed-down options to match the problems your team really runs into.
Put the sprint or project name in the link as a hidden field, so the first question fills itself.
Share the link a day before the retro and read the answers in the dashboard while you prepare.

faqs.q: What questions should I ask in a retrospective?
faqs.a: What went well, what slowed you down, and what to try next are the core three. Comparing with the previous period and asking about psychological safety add useful depth.

faqs.q: Why run a retrospective survey before the meeting?
faqs.a: People answer more honestly on their own, and quieter team members get the same voice as the loudest. The meeting then starts with real input instead of a blank board.
It often helps, especially in teams where people are new or there's tension. Don't add a name question unless the team agrees to it.

faqs.q: Can I use this for project retrospectives, not just sprints?
faqs.a: Yes. The first question names the period, so it works for a sprint, a launch, a quarter or a whole project.

doc.title: Team retrospective
doc.description: Collect everyone's view of a sprint or project before the retro meeting.

blocks.title: Retro time. Answer on your own before we meet, so we can spend the meeting on what matters.
Which sprint, project or period is this for?
How did this stretch of work feel for you?
Did we deliver what we set out to do?
What went well that we should keep doing?
What slowed you down? Pick all that apply.
Pick the biggest thing that got in the way. What happened?
Compared with last time, how did we do on these?
What's one thing we should try next time?
How comfortable did you feel raising problems during this period?
What would make it easier to speak up? You can keep this general.
Anyone you'd like to thank for something specific?
